title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Graph-Paper Notebook. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Graph-Paper Notebook
options.lineage: Colombian cuaderno cuadriculado, corrected in class
options.thesis: Your draft lives on a squared notebook page; feedback arrives the way a teacher marks it: highlighter, margin notes, a circled score.
materials: 5 mm squared paper with a red margin rule
four highlighter colours, one per part
options.viewport: One notebook sheet fills the screen: the paragraph is written on the grid, each part swiped in its highlighter colour; the wide left margin carries the part labels and word budget; the score is circled in red pen at the top right.
options.risk: Can tip into skeuomorphic costume if paper texture, fake handwriting or page curls creep in; the grid and pen marks must stay functional.

raised.raise: Feedback is set in the margin and bracketed back to the exact part it is about, never in a detached card.
The 190–210 word budget is a ruled track filled part by part (25 / 50 / 100 / 25), so overflow is visible like a tape that will not fit.
Every number (words, sentences, scores) is set in tabular figures in fixed columns, so counts never jitter while typing.
The part you are working on burns at full colour; the other three drop to a quiet tint.

options.label: The Class Deck
options.lineage: the Week 4 slides students already saw
options.thesis: The app speaks the exact language of the slides: numbered 01–04 part chips, navy ink, ✓/✗ verdict tags.
options.viewport: A clean two-pane editor: parts on the left as numbered slide-style blocks, verdicts and feedback on the right.
options.risk: Familiar and safe: closest to what most AI writing tools look like, with the slide colours as the only signature.

options.label: Annotated Edition
options.lineage: wide-margin reference editions with a centre rail
options.thesis: The paragraph set as a small text block inside a wide annotation margin where every comment is ruled back to its line.
options.viewport: Centred text block, feedback notes hung in the margins with hairline brackets to their sentences.
options.case: Excellent for product clarity (feedback tied to text) but reads as a scholarly book, not a student's own work.
options.risk: Feels academic-precious; weak on phones where margins vanish.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.lineage: hand-lettered cassette inlays timed to fill a side
options.thesis: Four parts as a tracklist that must fit exactly 190–210 words, like a side of tape.
options.viewport: A folded card: parts listed as tracks with word counts right-aligned and the total budget on the spine.
options.case: The word-budget metaphor is perfect; students in 2026 do not identify with cassettes.
options.risk: Nostalgia costume for an audience that never owned tapes.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Four coloured lines, one per part, meeting at interchanges.
options.viewport: Parts as stations along a line.
options.case: A paragraph is linear text, not a network; the map adds a layer to decode.
options.kept: The active part burns brightest; the rest recede.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Text as data columns and barcodes.
options.case: Hostile to a nervous B2 writer; no colour for the four parts.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One part per full screen, snap to the next.
options.viewport: One part fills the phone; swipe up for the next.
options.case: Students know it by heart, but it hides the whole paragraph, which the rubric judges as one unit.
options.kept: One part owns the focus at a time.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: Single type size, rank by weight and rule.
options.case: No connection to students' world; the rake fights text editing.
options.kept: State as a mark in a fixed cell: filled done, hollow pending.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS writing assistant (Grammarly / Notion-style), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Editor in the centre, AI feedback in a right sidebar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other AI writing tool.
